criterion: M2 exit criterion 11 (ROADMAP.md): outlines and toon ramps
setup: CPU renderer, 512 x 512. Scene S: a UV sphere (radius 1, 96 x 48 segments) on the optical axis 4 units from the eye, fovy 0.8, so its silhouette projects to a circle whose radius in pixels is known in closed form. Scene K: a unit cube seen from a corner direction, whose three visible creases project to known segments. References are analytic, never a second rendering.
metric: edge distance: for a set of edge pixels E and an analytic curve R, (a) precision: every pixel centre in E lies within d of R; (b) coverage: R sampled every 0.25 px has an E pixel centre within d at every sample.

depth_edges.bound: precision and coverage at d = 1.5 px

id_edges.scene: S plus a second sphere (radius 2.5, 8 units from the eye) centred behind it on the same axis, ids 1 and 2; both silhouettes are circles
id_edges.reference: the union of the two silhouette circles: near against far, and far against the background
id_edges.bound: precision and coverage at d = 1.5 px

normal_edges.bound: precision and coverage at d = 1.5 px, counting only pixels inside the cube's silhouette (2 px in from it)

inverted_hull.scene: S with a hull of thickness 0.05
inverted_hull.reference: the annulus between the silhouettes of radius 1 and 1.05
inverted_hull.bound: every hull pixel within 1 px of the annulus; at least 99% of pixels whose centres lie in the annulus are hull pixels

toon_ramp.scene: S lit by one directional light, 4 bands
toon_ramp.reference: the band index from the exact sphere normal at each pixel (ray-sphere intersection)
toon_ramp.bound: at most 2% of covered pixels differ, and every differing pixel lies within 1.5 px of an analytic band boundary

control: each check also runs on a deliberately wrong input (the silhouette radius scaled by 1.02, the crease set rotated by one cube edge, the hull thickness doubled, the light direction negated) and must fail
does_not_prove: How the outlines look in a game, their GPU twins (not built yet), or stability under camera motion.
amended: 2026-10-10, before the first run: the id_edges scene and reference made exact (two concentric silhouettes); the earlier text omitted the far sphere's own edge, which is an id edge
